E1.evidence: The report gives a full runtime log from bt_navigator, controller_server and planner_server with the failing sequence, and the maintainer diagnoses it: "That occurs here [1], so the server timeout doesn't cancel the action in time." -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/4659#issuecomment-2327562456 . A second user reports the same halt error on Jazzy and that raising the timeout removes it: "Increasing `default_server_timeout` from 30 to even ~50ms solves this issue." -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/4659#issuecomment-2607122040

E2.evidence: bt_navigator (its nav2_behavior_tree BtActionNode FollowPath client) and controller_server (the follow_path action server) are separate nodes that interact only through the follow_path action. The failure depends on timing that crosses that boundary: the client waits for the server's goal acknowledgement and for the cancel result only for server_timeout (reporter: "Our `server_timeout` is currently set to 100ms." -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/4659#issuecomment-2340126891), and when the server's response arrives later the client gives up while the server keeps executing. Maintainer: "If you have a server timeout of 10ms and you've just started a planning request that is 100ms in length, then it won't always cancel in time." -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/4659#issuecomment-2327562456 . The resolving edit (PR #5895) adds a separate cancel timeout parameter to the client; it is not a name binding, build change, or firmware fault.

E3.evidence: PAIR: bt_navigator sends follow_path goals and cancel requests to controller_server and consumes its goal acknowledgement and result ("[bt_navigator-12] [INFO]: Starting path following\r\n[controller_server-8] [INFO]: Received a goal, begin computing control effort." -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/4659).

E4.evidence: Observed: "The `bt_navigator` gets a `Failed to get result for compute_path_to_pose in node halt!` or a `Failed to get result for follow_path in node halt!` error, and the `controller_server` keeps on trying to follow the last received path." -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/4659

failed_conditions.quote: [bt_navigator-12] [WARN]: Timed out while waiting for action server to acknowledge goal request for follow_path
[bt_navigator-12] [ERROR]: Failed to get result for follow_path in node halt!

loudness_evidence: The only diagnostics are runtime log lines printed by bt_navigator's own BT node code ("Timed out while waiting for action server to acknowledge goal request for follow_path", "Failed to get result for follow_path in node halt!"); no build, connection or activation diagnostic from existing tooling. The effect is wrong motion: "the `controller_server` keeps on trying to follow the last received path." -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/4659

resolution.summary: PR #5895 adds a separate cancel timeout (blackboard key cancel_timeout, bt_navigator parameter default_cancel_timeout, default 50 ms) and uses it instead of server_timeout when BtActionNode::halt() waits for the cancelled goal's result. controller_server is unchanged. The goal-acknowledgement timeout path (condition 1) is not changed by the fix.
resolution.evidence: Merged into main as 640196af92900d073390b07bcd81935d486fd3bb and closes #4659; the reporter never confirmed it in the Iron composition. Related working observation with a different peer/distro (Jazzy, coverage navigator) using the timeout workaround: "Increasing `default_server_timeout` from 30 to even ~50ms solves this issue." -- https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/4659#issuecomment-2607122040

notes: Class `other` is used for both conditions because the mismatch is a server response latency exceeding the client's wait timeout on an action; none of the listed classes fits (qos_deadline is the DDS deadline policy, rate_shortfall concerns a periodic publication rate). Condition 1 mechanism per a commenter: after the acknowledgement timeout the client resets future_goal_handle_ with goal_handle_ unset, so halt()'s should_cancel_goal() returns false and the follow_path goal is never cancelled (https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/4659#issuecomment-2556526828); the maintainer calls this "a different issue" from the cancel-timeout problem (https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/4659#issuecomment-2616870937). Other composition in the same report, not specified here: bt_navigator -> planner_server over action compute_path_to_pose ("[bt_navigator-12] [ERROR]: Failed to get result for compute_path_to_pose in node halt!"), which the maintainer attributes to Iron planners not checking cancel requests inside their planning loop (fixed on Jazzy+ through a cancel checker in the planner plugin API, not backportable). A commenter also mentions a hypothetical second publisher on cmd_vel from a recovery branch; not observed. The resolved composition pairs a main-branch bt_navigator with the Iron 1.2.9 controller_server only because the rule keeps unchanged units at their broken revision; no such deployment was reported.
